{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-26, dev_reflow2 hub session:

"Can't you just configure reflow2 client in command line? Something like "reflow2 --client=local" or "reflow2 --client=remote api.flo2.io". Then if you want to switch from remote back to local, just run "reflow2 --client=local" and vice-versa. Then every time you run cd project_x and then run Claude, the reflow2 is already configured when you setup reflow2. Then the reflow2 client handles everything whether that be ti the local or remote...the agent never knows or cares"

WHAT IT ANSWERS: the default flo2's dec:idea-a-terminal-agent-starts-a-new-design-on-flo2 found missing ("in an empty folder, local or remote is a choice somebody has to have made"). One setting, kept in the person's own configuration, read by reflow2's local client (req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url), which is registered once for every folder. The agent talks to the same stdio server either way.

THE SHAPE, as far as it goes today:
- `reflow2 --client=remote https://api.flo2.io` records the server AND is where the one-time sign-in happens (browser or device code), or where a key the person opts into is stored. Like `gh auth login`.
- `reflow2 --client=local` goes back to local, the default (req:reflow2-keeps-working-entirely-on-one-machine).
- Every `claude` afterwards finds reflow2 already configured; /genesis in an empty folder creates the design wherever the setting says.

═══ PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT ═══
· 🛑 A GLOBAL SWITCH MUST NOT MOVE A FOLDER THAT ALREADY HAS A DESIGN. If project_x's design is on flo2.io and the switch flips to local, project_x's next session would open an EMPTY local store, and the empty-design nudge (settled: offer the move, never adopt) is all that stands between that and a second, divergent copy. So the switch should decide only for folders with NO design yet. A folder with a pointer file follows its pointer; a folder with a local store stays local. What the folder already holds always wins over the setting.
· SWITCHING MOVES NOTHING. `--client=local` after working remotely does not bring designs home, and `--client=remote` does not send one up. Moving a design is the separate, deliberate import (dec:idea-a-repo-that-holds-its-design-moves-it-to-a-remote-server-once).
· A RUNNING SESSION KEEPS WHAT IT HAS. The setting is read when the client starts; flipping it mid-session changes the next session, not the current one.
· THE EXACT WORDS ARE OPEN: `reflow2 --client=...`, `reflow2 use local|remote <url>`, `reflow2 login <url>`. The behaviour above matters more than the spelling.

═══ 2026-09-26 — ANTHONY ADDS THE KEY TO THE SAME SETUP COMMAND, RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING ═══
Anthony: "Could you also add the api_key when you set up the client: "reflow2 --client=remote https://api.flo2.io --api-key some-api-key-abcde" or reflow2 --client=remote https://api.flo2.io --api-key FLO2_API_KEY" where FLO2_API_KEY is an env car with the API key? Then do the login once there. The API key then is linked to you as a user and only your designs (or those that have been shared with you) show up. If flo2.io supports web based login, then the API key here is not needed, but for people not using a flo2.io as their remote, having this initial setup is good to have"

So the setup command takes ONE of: a sign-in (for a server that offers one, like flo2.io), or a key (for a server that hands out keys, like an organization's shared reflow2). Either way it happens once, and the client carries it on every request afterwards. This matches req:a-local-client-works-against-a-remote-reflow2-server-by-url, which already lists "a key or token the person supplies ... read from an environment variable, a file or the OS keychain".

═══ PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT ═══
· 🛑 A KEY TYPED ON THE COMMAND LINE LEAKS. `--api-key some-api-key-abcde` is saved in the shell's history file, and is visible to other processes while the command runs. Safer forms for the same step: name the environment variable rather than pass its value (a separate flag such as `--api-key-env FLO2_API_KEY`, so the client reads it itself), or prompt for the key without echoing it, or read it from stdin. Then store it in the OS keychain, so the environment variable can be removed afterwards.
· `--api-key FLO2_API_KEY` IS AMBIGUOUS: the client cannot tell a variable's name from a key that happens to look like one. Two distinct flags, or a prefix, keep it unambiguous.
· "ONLY YOUR DESIGNS SHOW UP" IS THE SERVER'S JOB, NOT THE CLIENT'S. On flo2.io the key maps to one account, and its memberships decide what it reaches, exactly as with the sign-in (req:no-user-api-keys: never required, but a technical person may opt in). On an organization's own server, reflow2 itself authenticates nothing, so that promise holds only if the organization's front layer maps each key to a person and enforces what they reach. The client can carry a key; it cannot make a server honour one.
· Revoking or rotating a key should be one command too (e.g. `reflow2 --client=remote <url> --api-key-env NEW_KEY` replaces the stored one), so a leaked key is not a reason to reinstall.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — one command sets where reflow2 works (`reflow2 --client=local` / `reflow2 --client=remote api.flo2.io`), and the agent never knows or cares which","status":"proposed"}
